original_question: For a Coxeter system (W, S) and elements u <= v in W, is there always some Coxeter system (W', S') and some element w' in W' such that the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial P_{u,v}(q) equals P_{e', w'}(q), where e' is the identity of W'?
target_in_paper: Problem 32 in arXiv:2509.25446, under "2. Problems of 2025"; it is explicitly attributed there to [Bren2024, Problem 1.9] and is the exact source of the draft.
correct_elements: The draft already captures the core existence problem almost verbatim: for an arbitrary Coxeter system (W, S) and a comparable pair u ≤ v, it asks whether one can realize the same Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial as a lower-interval polynomial from the identity in some possibly different Coxeter system (W', S'). It also correctly distinguishes the identity element e' of the target system.
missing_details: The order relation u ≤ v should be stated to be the Bruhat order.
The polynomial meant is the ordinary Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial P_{u,v}(q) \in Z[q], i.e. the J = ∅ specialization of the parabolic family defined in Theorem 1.3 of Brenti's source paper.
The quantifiers are universal over all Coxeter systems (W, S) and all pairs u, v \in W with u ≤ v, and existential over some possibly different Coxeter system (W', S') and some w \in W'.
No finiteness assumption on W or W' is part of the stated problem; it ranges over arbitrary Coxeter systems.

To stay faithful to the paper's intent, it helps to make explicit that the target realization is specifically as a lower-interval polynomial P_{e,w}(q), which is stronger than merely realizing the same polynomial as some P_{x,y}(q).
A nearby contextual remark in the source paper is that the problem is not asking for W' = W; Brenti notes that the answer is easily negative under that stronger requirement.
refined_question: Let (W, S) be a Coxeter system, let ≤ denote the Bruhat order on W, and let P_{x,y}(q) \in Z[q] denote the ordinary Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial of W. For every pair u, v \in W with u ≤ v, does there exist a Coxeter system (W', S') and an element w \in W' such that P_{u,v}(q) = P_{e,w}(q), where e is the identity element of W'?
justification: The given arXiv paper is a notebook of open problems, and the draft matches its Problem 32 on PDF p. 3 essentially word-for-word. That notebook entry explicitly cites Brenti's Problem 1.9 as its source. Because Problem 32 itself is terse, the needed notation comes from Brenti's Section 1: Bruhat order is defined on PDF p. 1, and Theorem 1.3 on PDF p. 2 defines the parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials and identifies the ordinary Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials as the J = ∅ case. Brenti's Problem 1.9 on PDF p. 5 is the official formulation nearest to your draft, and the immediately following remark there explains that the version with W' forced to equal W is easily false. So the refined question should simply make the Bruhat-order and ordinary-KL-polynomial conventions explicit, without broadening beyond Problem 1.9/Problem 32.
